subject: Hosted API — Data Territory, TTL, and Erasure Procedures (Security Questionnaire)
messages:
From: Sanjay Mehra <sanjay@lynexpay.com>

Cc: security@lynexpay.com
Date: Thu, 20 Jun 2029 15:22:00 -0400
Subject: Data residency / retention questions for Hosted API

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for taking this. We're filling out our procurement security questionnaire and have a few targeted questions about Redwood's Hosted API data residency, retention, and deletion practices. We need concise, auditable answers we can include in our RFP appendix. Specific asks:

1) Where are customer request payloads and generated outputs stored by default? Are they geo-partitioned by customer?
2) What are default retention TTLs for request logs, model outputs, and analytics?
3) What's the documented process and timeline for complete erasure when a customer requests deletion (including backups and snapshots)?
4) Do you provide a deletion certificate or attestation we can retain?

Can you respond with a brief bullet-style reply and attach any operative playbooks or diagrams?

Appreciate it — we're targeting legal review next week.

Sanjay Mehra
Head of Security, LynexPay
sanjay@lynexpay.com

From: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Mehra <sanjay@lynexpay.com>
Cc: security@lynexpay.com
Date: Fri, 21 Jun 2029 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Data residency / retention questions for Hosted API

Sanjay — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, followed by implementation notes and references. Attaching: redwood_residency_map.pdf and deletion-playbook-v1.2.pdf.

1) Storage locations / geo-partitioning
- Primary request handling and ephemeral runtime caches (KV cache, prefix cache) are served from the region where the request is routed (by default US: us-west-2; EU customers can be pinned to eu-west-1).
- By default, we do not copy customer request payloads to other regions unless cross-region failover is invoked by routing policy.
- Long-term artifacts (billing metering, aggregated analytics) are stored in a regional data store. Customer tenants can be pinned to a primary region via our console; see attached residency map.

2) Default retention TTLs
- Runtime KV / prefix caches: ephemeral, TTL = 7 days (auto-evict based on usage).
- Request logs (for safety and debugging): default retention = 30 days. Redaction is applied to PII per our data-minimization rules unless logging is enabled for the tenant.
- Model outputs and generated text: not persisted beyond ephemeral serving unless tenant enables "persist logs" in console. If enabled, persisted outputs inherit the tenant's retention policy (default 90 days).
- Billing and metering records: retained for 13 months for accounting and invoice reconciliation.

3) Deletion / erasure process and timelines
- Deletion request received via the Console or support ticket triggers a three-phase workflow:
  a) Immediate: tenant flagged for deletion; writes to primary stores are blocked within 1 business hour.
  b) Primary purge: background purge job removes records from primary databases within 48 hours for standard data types (requests, generated text, user metadata).
  c) Snapshot & backups: snapshot lifecycle is 90 days; snapshots are overwritten on a 90-day rolling cycle. When a deletion is requested, we mark snapshot entries for scrubbing and the backup index is updated within 7 days; complete removal from snapshot backups occurs by the next overwrite cycle (<= 90 days).
- Encrypted backups: all backups are encrypted with a KMS key. For hosted tenants, we perform crypto-erase by rotating and securely disposing of the relevant key material when requested where applicable; this can accelerate effective data inaccessibility in some configurations.

4) Deletion attestation
- We provide a signed deletion attestation (PDF) upon completion of the deletion workflow and final snapshot scrub. We can deliver the attestation via DocuSign (sample link included).

Operational notes / controls
- We log every deletion request with an audit trail (requestor, timestamp, ticket ID).
- Customers on Dedicated/Private deployments receive additional options for shorter snapshot cycles and custom KMS key ownership.
- We support region pinning at onboarding; please confirm if LynexPay requires US-only residency.

If helpful I can forward this to our infra team to provide a short diagram of the purge job flow and an example audit record.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
Redwood Inference

Ben / Jonas — forwarding the inquiry from LynexPay (see thread above). I included our top-line answers and attached the playbook + residency map. Two asks:

- Ben: can you confirm the snapshot scrub timeline wording (I said "<= 90 days"). Is that safe to send as-is for hosted customers, or should it read "within one snapshot cycle (up to 90 days)"?
- Jonas: can you attach a sanitized example audit record (no PII) showing delete request logging and the ticket ID format? If available, please also confirm whether KMS crypto-erase is offered for hosted tenants or only Dedicated.

Thanks — need to get back to them by end of day PST.

—Vanessa
From: ben.carter@redwood.ai <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 21 Jun 2029 09:06:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Data residency / retention questions for Hosted API

Vanessa — quick confirmation: wording is fine. For hosted tenants the practical behavior is: snapshots are on a 90-day rolling retention and entries marked for deletion are excluded from restores and are scrubbed during the next overwrite window. Saying "by the next overwrite cycle (<= 90 days)" is accurate.

KMS crypto-erase: for hosted we can perform key rotation and crypto-erase where the tenant uses our managed KMS; for customers with customer-managed keys (Dedicated/Private) they control key destruction. I'll attach a sanitized audit example to Jonas in thread.

—Ben
